title: Assessment of Cas9 Activity in Cancer Cell Lines
author: Verity Goodwin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgvtjw6n
materials: If cells are >90% confluent, passage each well:
Follow "Fixing cell pellets" protocol found here: https://protocols.io/view/fixing-cell-pellets-bg2fjybn.html

steps.title: Detach and collect Cas9 cells
steps.instruction: Detach and collect Cas9 cells following steps 1‑8 of the protocol “Passaging adherent cancer cell lines” (https://protocols.io/view/passaging-adherent-cancer-cell-lines-bgtbjwin.html).

steps.title: Prepare cell suspension (version 1)
steps.instruction: Prepare a suspension of 1 × 10⁶ cells in 7.2 mL complete media (equivalent to 2.5 × 10⁶ cells per well when 1.8 mL is used).

steps.title: Prepare cell suspension (version 2)
steps.instruction: Prepare a suspension of 1 × 10⁶ cells in 7.2 mL complete media (equivalent to 2.5 × 10⁵ cells per well when 1.8 mL is used).

steps.title: Add polybrene
steps.instruction: Add 6.4 µL polybrene (final concentration 8 µg/mL) to the cell suspension and mix using a 10 mL stripette and a pipetboy.

steps.title: Distribute cells into wells
steps.instruction: Transfer 1.8 mL of the cell suspension into each of three wells of a 6‑well plate (mock, control, reporter). For each well add 1.6 µL polybrene, 1.8 mL cell suspension and 200 µL of the appropriate media/virus as shown in Table 1. Label the plate as in Figure 1.

steps.title: Add media or virus to wells
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL fresh media to the mock well; add 200 µL of the designated control virus (BFP/GFP) to the control well; add 200 µL of the reporter virus (BFP/GFP/gGFP) to the reporter well. Mix gently by rocking the plate.

steps.title: Incubate plate
steps.instruction: Place the 6‑well plate in the incubator.

steps.title: Add fresh media (Day 2)
steps.instruction: If cells are to receive 2 mL fresh media per well, add 2 mL fresh complete media to each well without dislodging the cells.

steps.title: Wash wells with PBS
steps.instruction: Aspirate culture media from each well. Add 2 mL PBS to each well by angling the pipette at the side of the well. Aspirate the PBS.

steps.title: Add TrypLE and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL TrypLE to each well and incubate in the incubator for 3–5 min. Observe under a microscope; if cells remain attached, return to the incubator for a few more minutes until fully detached.

steps.title: Neutralize TrypLE and resuspend
steps.instruction: When cells are detached, add 500 µL complete media to each well, mix by pipetting up and down with a P1000, and wash the well base to ensure all cells are detached.

steps.title: Pellet cells and split
steps.instruction: Carefully aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet. Resuspend each pellet in a volume of media appropriate for a 1:2 or 1:3 split ratio, depending on growth rate, and discard excess cells.

steps.title: Collect cell sample for flow
steps.instruction: Collect 1 mL of the cell suspension into a labelled 1.5 mL centrifuge tube and centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min at °C (temperature not specified) using a minifuge inside the MSC.

steps.title: Passage at 90 % confluence (Day 3)
steps.instruction: If cells are >90 % confluent, passage at a 1:2 split ratio following steps 7.1‑7.5 of the referenced passaging protocol.

steps.title: Fix cells (Day 4)
steps.instruction: Detach and collect cells following steps 7.1‑7.4 of the referenced protocol. Carefully aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Configure flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Set up the cytometer to record FSC‑A, FSC‑W, SSC‑A, 450/50‑A (BFP) and 530/30‑A (GFP) channels.

steps.title: Acquire mock sample
steps.instruction: Run the mock sample first. Use FSC‑A vs SSC‑A to gate debris and FSC‑A vs FSC‑W to gate single cells with a polygon gate; adjust FSC and SSC voltages if needed. Verify that mock cells are negative for BFP (450/50, 405‑A) and GFP (530/30, 488‑A) by placing a polygon gate on the negative population (left side). Record 10 000 events.

steps.title: Acquire control sample
steps.instruction: Run the control sample (BFP⁺/GFP⁺ cells) and record 10 000 events.

steps.title: Acquire reporter sample
steps.instruction: Run the reporter sample and record 10 000 events.

steps.title: Export .fcs files
steps.instruction: Export the .fcs files and analyze them using appropriate analysis software.

steps.title: Gate mock sample in FlowJo
steps.instruction: Open the mock file in FlowJo (or equivalent). Draw a gate around the main population in FSC‑A vs SSC‑A, double‑click to open a new pane, draw a gate around single cells in FSC‑A vs FSC‑W, change the axis to BFP vs SSC‑A and draw a BFP⁺ gate based on the negative cells.

steps.title: Apply gates to control sample
steps.instruction: Copy the BFP⁺ gate (and other gates) to the control sample and verify that it identifies BFP⁺ cells.

steps.title: Apply gates to reporter sample
steps.instruction: Copy all gates to the reporter sample. Ensure the Cas9 gate does not include any GFP⁺ cells; the majority should be BFP⁺ GFP⁻. Pass criteria: ≥75 % Cas9 positivity.

steps.title: Define Cas9‑positive gate
steps.instruction: In the reporter (or control) sample, double‑click the BFP⁺ gate, change the plot axis to BFP vs GFP, gate the BFP⁺ GFP⁻ region and name this gate “Cas9”.
